'''''Passiflora vesicaria''''' is a [[species]] of plant in the family [[Passifloraceae]].<ref name="inaturalist-Passiflora vesicaria">{{cite web |title=Passiflora vesicaria |url=https://www.inaturalist.org/taxa/1438095-Passiflora-vesicaria |website=iNaturalist |access-date=2023-08-09 |language=en}}</ref> It was first described by Linnaeus, later synonymized with ''[[Passiflora foetida]]'' as the varieties ''Passiflora foetida'' var. ''glabrifolia'', ''P. foetida'' var. ''hispida'', and ''P. foetida'' var. ''isthmia''.<ref name="A revision of Passiflora section Dysosima: Passifloraceae">{{cite journal |title=A revision of Passiflora section Dysosima: Passifloraceae | url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/45066258 |journal=Curtis's Botanical Magazine | jstor=45066258 |access-date=2023-08-09 |language=en | last1=Vanderplank | first1=John | date=2013 | volume=30 | issue=4 | pages=318–387 | doi=10.1111/curt.12050 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> Vanderplank restored it to full species status in 2013.<ref name="A revision of Passiflora section Dysosmia: Passifloraceae">{{cite journal |title=A revision of Passiflora section Dysosima: Passifloraceae | url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/45066258 |journal=Curtis's Botanical Magazine | jstor=45066258 |access-date=2023-08-09 |language=en | last1=Vanderplank | first1=John | date=2013 | volume=30 | issue=4 | pages=318–387 | doi=10.1111/curt.12050 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Description==
Like most ''Passiflora'' species, ''P. vesicaria'' is a climbing vine. The leaves are three-lobed with a serrate margin; the flowers are solitary with pinnatisect bracts and the corona in several rings.<ref name="World Flora Online">{{cite web |title=Passiflora vesicaria L. |url=https://www.worldfloraonline.org/taxon/wfo-0001090911 |website=World Flora Online |access-date=2023-08-09 |language=en}}</ref> It is distinguished from ''P. foetida'' by having hairless to sparsely-haired fruit that ripen to yellow-orange to orange instead of hairy fruit that remain greenish when fully ripe.<ref name="A revision of Passiflora section Dysosima: Passifloraceae">{{cite journal |title=A revision of Passiflora section Dysosima: Passifloraceae | url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/45066258 |journal=Curtis's Botanical Magazine | jstor=45066258 |access-date=2023-08-09 |language=en | last1=Vanderplank | first1=John | date=2013 | volume=30 | issue=4 | pages=318–387 | doi=10.1111/curt.12050 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Range==
''Passiflora vesicaria'' is native to Central and South America, including Brazil, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, Venezuela, Suriname, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama and Costa Rica; and to several Caribbean islands including Trinidad and Tobago, the Windward Islands, Leeward Islands, Puerto Rico,  Jamaica, and Cuba.<ref name="kew">{{cite web |title=''Passiflora vesicaria'' L. |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:675582-1 |website=POWO |access-date=2023-08-09 |language=en}}</ref> The variety ''P. vesicaria'' var. ''galapagensis'' is endemic to the [[Galapagos Islands]].<ref name="A revision of Passiflora section Dysosima: Passifloraceae">{{cite journal |title=A revision of Passiflora section Dysosima: Passifloraceae | url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/45066258 |journal=Curtis's Botanical Magazine | jstor=45066258 |access-date=2023-08-09 |language=en | last1=Vanderplank | first1=John | date=2013 | volume=30 | issue=4 | pages=318–387 | doi=10.1111/curt.12050 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

It has been introduced in Florida in the United States,<ref name="Passiflora vesicaria">{{cite web |title=''Passiflora vesicaria'' |url=https://florida.plantatlas.usf.edu/Plant.aspx?id=5015 |website=Atlas of Florida Plants |access-date=2023-08-09 |language=en}}</ref> South and Southeast Asia,<ref name="Passiflora vesicaria L.">{{cite web |title=''Passiflora vesicaria L.''|url=https://www.gbif.org/species/3588353 |website=Global Biodiversity Information Facility |access-date=2025-01-20 |language=en}}</ref> and to many tropical islands worldwide, including Aldabra, Borneo, Caroline Is., Cook Is., Fiji, Gilbert Is., Marianas, Nauru, New Caledonia, and Wake I.<ref name="kew"/>

==Habitat==
''Passiflora vesicaria'' grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.<ref name="kew"/>

==Etymology==
''Passiflora'' is derived from the Italian ''passio'', meaning "suffering" and the Latin ''flora'' meaning "flower", in reference to the Passion of the Christ. ''Vesicaria'' means bladder, presumably referring to the form of the fruits.

==Taxonomy==
''Passiflora vesicaria'' contains the following varieties:
* ''Passiflora vesicaria'' var. ''vesicaria''<ref name="inaturalist-Passiflora vesicaria" />
* ''Passiflora vesicaria'' var. ''galapagensis''<ref name="inaturalist-Passiflora vesicaria" /> – [[Galápagos Islands]]
